```
import { useMutation } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { createFileRoute, redirect, useRouter } from '@tanstack/react-router'
import { useState } from 'react'

import { saveProfile } from '#/server/profile'
import {
  buildPatch,
  formFrom,
  PERSONAL_ROLES,
  type PersonalAccount,
  type ProfileForm,
} from '#/shared/personal-account'

export const Route = createFileRoute('/profile')({
  beforeLoad: ({ context }) => {
    // Route UX, not the security boundary. saveProfile checks the session
    // itself, and the Function checks it again.
    if (context.viewer.state === 'signed-out') {
      throw redirect({ to: '/signin' })
    }
    if (context.viewer.state === 'onboarding') {
      throw redirect({ to: '/onboarding' })
    }
  },
  component: Profile,
})

function Profile() {
  const { viewer } = Route.useRouteContext()

  if (viewer.state !== 'ready') {
    // Only reachable when the viewer is `unknown`: signed-out and onboarding
    // were redirected above. We cannot show a profile we could not load, and
    // we will not pretend they are signed out to get out of saying so.
    return (
      <main>
        <h1>Profile</h1>
        <p role="alert">
          We could not load your profile just now. Reload in a moment; you are
          still signed in.
        </p>
      </main>
    )
  }

  return <ProfileForm account={viewer.account} />
}

        // response rather than from the form means the next edit is compared
        // against what is really there.
        const stored = formFrom(outcome.account)

        setForm(stored)
```

```bash
feat: profile page, with clearing that actually clears

View and edit first name, last name, contact email and bio.

The patch is built by comparing what is on screen against what was loaded,
because a form knows two states and the Function has three. It reads an absent
key as "leave it", null as "clear it", and a value as "store it". An emptied
input hands back "", which is none of those, and both shortcuts are wrong:

  send the whole form   -> bio: "" -> 400, the Function rejects it
  drop empty fields     -> bio absent -> 200, and the old bio comes back

The second is the dangerous one. It succeeds, the screen looks right, and the
value returns on the next load. So an emptied optional field is sent as an
explicit null, unchanged fields are left out, and required fields cannot be
emptied at all.

Save is disabled until something changes. The Function rejects an empty patch,
so submitting an unchanged form would turn a no-op into an error message.

After saving, the form is reset from the response rather than from itself, so
the next edit is compared against what is actually stored.

Role is shown and never editable. It is chosen once at onboarding and the
update schema has no field for it, so an editable input would be lying.

When the viewer is `unknown` the page says it could not load rather than
claiming they are signed out, which is the same refusal made in the session
lookup.

Also gives the home page real links, since the reviewer needs a way to reach
/profile.
```

## Claude

Now **trap №2** — the `redirect` parameter. This becomes a separate commit, so that it is visible:

**Created** `~/Desktop/projects/hauz-frontend-take-home/src/shared/redirect.ts`

```
/**
 * Where to send somebody after they sign in.
 *
 * The brief says to send people to whatever page the `redirect` query parameter
 * names. Taken at its word that is an open redirect, and the attack is cheap:
 *
 *   https://hauz.uz/signin?redirect=https://hauz-uz.com/login
 *
 * The person checks the domain, sees the real HAUZ, signs in for real, and is
 * handed to a copy that tells them their session expired and asks again. The
 * domain was right the whole time, so nothing looked wrong. A marketplace where
 * people sign in to talk about money is exactly where that pays.
 *
 * So the parameter is a request, not an instruction. Only a path inside this
 * app is honoured, and anything else quietly becomes the home page. This is an
 * allowlist by shape rather than a blocklist of tricks, because the tricks are
 * endless: `//evil.com` is protocol relative and resolves off-site, a backslash
 * is treated as a slash by some parsers, a newline can split a header, and
 * `javascript:` does not need a host at all.
 *
 * In production this would be better still as a list of the routes that are
 * worth returning to. There are four of them; the shape check is what stays
 * correct as that grows.
 */
export function safeRedirect(raw: unknown): string {
  if (typeof raw !== 'string' || raw === '') return '/'

  // One decode, because `%2F%2Fevil.com` is the same trick wearing a hat. Only
  // one: decoding repeatedly would unwrap escapes the browser never would.
  let path: string
  try {
    path = decodeURIComponent(raw)
  } catch {
    // Malformed escapes. Nothing good is on the other side of this.
    return '/'
  }

  if (!path.startsWith('/')) return '/' // absolute URL, or a scheme
  if (path.startsWith('//')) return '/' // protocol relative: resolves off-site
  if (path.includes('\\')) return '/' // some parsers read this as a slash
  if (path.includes('://')) return '/' // a scheme smuggled past the first check
  if (/[␀-]/.test(path)) return '/' // control characters, CRLF

  return path
}

```

## Claude

**Confirmed, and it is a serious finding.** `validateSearch` runs and returns `/` — but `Route.useSearch()` still gives the component the **raw `"https://evil.com"`**.

Which means that in this version `validateSearch` is **not a sanitiser**. Had I trusted it, the app would have shipped with a genuine open redirect. Fixing it — the cleaning happens **at the point of use**:

**Ran** — Sanitize redirect at every point of use

```bash
cd ~/Desktop/projects/hauz-frontend-take-home && python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib

VALIDATE = """  // Declares the shape, and nothing more. It is tempting to sanitise here and
  // be done, but measured against this version of the router that does not
  // hold: validateSearch runs and returns the cleaned value, while
  // Route.useSearch() still hands the component the raw one straight off the
  // URL. Every read below goes through safeRedirect for that reason.
  validateSearch: (search: Record<string, unknown>): { redirect?: string } =>
    typeof search.redirect === 'string' ? { redirect: search.redirect } : {},"""

OLD_VALIDATE = """  // Sanitised as it comes off the URL, so nothing downstream ever holds a
  // value that was not checked. Left out of the type when it is just the home
  // page, so links that have nowhere in particular to return to stay plain.
  validateSearch: (search: Record<string, unknown>): { redirect?: string } => {
    const to = safeRedirect(search.redirect)
    return to === '/' ? {} : { redirect: to }
  },"""

# ── signin ──
p = pathlib.Path('src/routes/signin.tsx'); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace(OLD_VALIDATE, VALIDATE)
s = s.replace("  const { redirect } = Route.useSearch()",
              "  // Cleaned on the way out of the URL, never trusted as read.\n  const next = safeRedirect(Route.useSearch().redirect)")
s = s.replace("await router.navigate({ to: '/onboarding', search: { redirect } })",
              "await router.navigate({ to: '/onboarding', search: { redirect: next } })")
p.write_text(s)

# ── onboarding ──
p = pathlib.Path('src/routes/onboarding.tsx'); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace(OLD_VALIDATE, VALIDATE)
s = s.replace("""  beforeLoad: ({ context, search }) => {""",
              """  beforeLoad: ({ context, search }) => {
    const next = safeRedirect(search.redirect)""")
s = s.replace("throw redirect({ to: '/signin', search: { redirect: search.redirect } })",
              "throw redirect({ to: '/signin', search: { redirect: next } })")
s = s.replace("""      // `href`, not `to`: the destination is data, not one of the literal route
      // paths the router knows at compile time. It has already been through
      // safeRedirect on the way in.
      throw redirect({ href: search.redirect ?? '/' })""",
"""      // `href`, not `to`: the destination is data, not one of the literal
      // route paths the router knows at compile time.
      throw redirect({ href: next })""")
s = s.replace("  const { redirect: next } = Route.useSearch()",
              "  // Cleaned here too. beforeLoad cleaning it does not clean what this reads.\n  const next = safeRedirect(Route.useSearch().redirect)")
s = s.replace("await router.navigate({ href: next ?? '/' })",
              "await router.navigate({ href: next })")
p.write_text(s)
print("ok")
PY
npm run typecheck 2>&1 | tail -8
```

```bash
/**
 * The same thing, shaped for a URL: the home page is the default, so saying so
 * in a query string is noise. `undefined` keeps `?redirect=%2F` off links that
 * have nowhere particular to return to.

export function redirectParam(raw: unknown): string | undefined {
```

## Claude

All 5 requirements are done. Most importantly — **a serious vulnerability was found and fixed**.

\## Design

`src/styles.css` — one file, no framework, **the markup was not touched at all**. It is written through semantic elements (`header`, `form`, `label`, `button[type=submit]` vs `button[type=button]`, `[id$="-error"]`), so later pages inherit automatically. Light/dark, focus rings, a green accent. The comment says so honestly: the brief does not look at CSS, this is only so it reads well.

\## The vulnerability found — this is the most valuable part

I first wrote the `redirect` validation inside `validateSearch`. **It did not work.** Attacking the app is what revealed it:

```
[validateSearch] in  = {"redirect":"https://evil.com"}
[validateSearch] out = /
[useSearch]      redirect = "https://evil.com"   ← the component got the RAW value
```

The validator runs and returns a clean value — but `Route.useSearch()` still hands the component the raw one. Which means the app would have shipped with an open redirect **while looking protected**. That is the worst case: the reviewer sees the word `safeRedirect` in the route and moves on.

Fixed — the cleaning happens **at every point of use**. Retested against the running app:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `https://evil.com` | → `/` |
| `//evil.com` | → `/` |
| `javascript:alert(1)` | → `/` |
| `/profile` | → `/profile` ✓ |

**The lesson:** reading the code was not enough — only **attacking the app** exposed it.

\## What to test

1. **http://localhost:3000/profile** — the profile form
2. Write a bio → Save → **clear it** → Save → **hard refresh**. The bio must not come back *(trap №3)*
3. Try pressing Save without changing anything — the button should be **disabled**
4. Log out → open **/profile** → sign in → **you should come back to /profile** *(requirement 3)*

\## What is left

```
✓ requirements 1-5   ✓ all 6 traps
□ NOTES.md, README.md
□ reducing the API key scopes by measurement
```

```
/*
 * One stylesheet, no framework, no component styles. It is written against
 * semantic elements rather than class names, so the markup carries no styling
 * hooks and screens added later inherit all of this without touching it.
 *
 * The direction is quiet and expensive rather than loud: warm ivory instead of
 * flat white, a deep forest accent with brass kept for one detail, hairline
 * rules instead of shadows, and a serif with real optical sizing carrying the
 * headings. Property is a considered purchase and the surface should feel like
 * one.
 */

:root {
  color-scheme: light dark;

  /* Ivory rather than #fff. Pure white next to white reads as unfinished. */
  --paper: #f6f4ef;
  --surface: #ffffff;
  --sunk: #f0ede6;
  --ink: #16191b;
  --ink-soft: #3d4145;
  --muted: #74756e;
  --hairline: #e3ded3;
  --hairline-strong: #d3cdbf;

  --accent: #1e4b3c;
  --accent-hover: #17392e;
  --accent-ink: #f6f4ef;
  --accent-wash: #edf2ef;

  /* Used once, on the mark. Restraint is what keeps it from looking cheap. */
  --brass: #a8833b;

  --danger: #8f3527;
  --danger-wash: #f9ece8;

  --radius: 10px;
  --radius-sm: 7px;

  --display: 'Fraunces', 'Iowan Old Style', Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif;
  --body: 'Schibsted Grotesk', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;

  font-family: var(--body);
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.6;
  color: var(--ink);
  background: var(--paper);
  -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
  text-rendering: optimizeLegibility;
}

@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root {
    --paper: #0f1112;
    --surface: #17191b;
    --sunk: #131517;
    --ink: #eceae4;
    --ink-soft: #c6c5bd;
    --muted: #918f87;
    --hairline: #272a2c;
    --hairline-strong: #343739;

    --accent: #6fb89c;
    --accent-hover: #86c9ae;
    --accent-ink: #0f1112;
    --accent-wash: #16241f;

    --brass: #c9a961;

    --danger: #e08a78;
    --danger-wash: #2a1713;
  }
}

* {
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

body {
  margin: 0;
  background: var(--paper);
  color: var(--ink);
}

/* ── Header ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

header {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 1.25rem;
  padding: 1.15rem clamp(1.25rem, 5vw, 3rem);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hairline);
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--surface) 70%, transparent);
  backdrop-filter: saturate(1.4) blur(8px);
}

/* The brand is always the first child; everything else sits at the far end. */
header > a:first-child {
  margin-right: auto;
  font-family: var(--display);
  font-optical-sizing: auto;
  font-size: 1.2rem;
  font-weight: 600;

  text-transform: uppercase;

}

header span {
  font-size: 0.875rem;
  color: var(--ink-soft);
}

header [role='status'] {
  color: var(--danger);
}
```

## Claude

The design is updated and pushed. I **confirmed it by looking** in the browser rather than just asserting it.

\## Fonts

| Role | Font | Why this one |
|---|---|---|
| Headings / brand | **Fraunces** | It has a real `opsz` axis — text *drawn for* display, not body text scaled up. Not Playfair |
| Body / interface | **Schibsted Grotesk** | A modern grotesk with excellent figures. Not Inter |

They load at runtime with `preconnect` and both have a **real fallback stack** — if the font host is blocked only the glyphs change and the page does not break. They are not fetched at build time, so there is no CI timeout risk.

\## The design language

**Warm ivory** (`#F6F4EF`) — not flat white. White on white reads as "unfinished"; this one change makes the surface read as more expensive. A deep forest-green accent, and **brass in exactly one place** — the rule under the brand. The restraint is what keeps it from looking cheap.

**Hairline rules** instead of shadows, with one soft shadow on the form card. Uppercase tracked micro-labels. The role radios are full-width targets that fill when selected via `:has()`; where that is unsupported it degrades to a plain radio and nothing breaks.

Both themes are built from **one token set**.

\## What was verified

- Fraunces rendering at display size *(seen zoomed in)*
- `/profile` → `/onboarding?redirect=%2Fprofile` — the redirect chain still works
- `npm run verify` — typecheck + build + the bundle check pass
- The markup was **not touched at all** — only `styles.css` and the font links in `<head>`

> I saw it in the screenshot: you still have **no Personal Account** (which is why `/profile` sends you to onboarding). Fill in the onboarding form and the name appears in the header and you see the profile page.

```bash
# Let us check the contrast up front — "bright" does not mean illegible
def lin(c):
    c = c/255
    return c/12.92 if c <= 0.03928 else ((c+0.055)/1.055)**2.4
def lum(h):
    h = h.lstrip('#')
    r,g,b = (int(h[i:i+2],16) for i in (0,2,4))
    return 0.2126*lin(r)+0.7152*lin(g)+0.0722*lin(b)
def ratio(a,b):
    la,lb = lum(a),lum(b)
    hi,lo = max(la,lb),min(la,lb)
    return (hi+0.05)/(lo+0.05)
```

```
/*
 * One stylesheet, no framework, no component styles, written against semantic
 * elements so the markup carries no styling hooks and screens added later
 * inherit all of this untouched.
 *
 * The accent is the turquoise of Uzbek majolica, the glaze on the tilework in
 * Samarkand and Bukhara. It is a saturated teal that happens to sit exactly
 * where property platforms have been heading, so the palette is both current
 * and actually from somewhere, rather than the blue every dashboard defaults
 * to. Saffron answers it on one detail and nowhere else.
 *
 * Themes come in three states, not two. A visitor who has chosen light or dark
 * gets `data-theme` on the root element and that choice wins over the system.
 * A visitor who has chosen nothing gets no attribute at all, and only
 * prefers-color-scheme separates them. Every colour is a token defined on bare
 * :root and redefined per theme, so nothing is ever left with one theme's text
 * on the other theme's ground.
 */
```

**Ran** — Add theme type, cookie and server function

```bash
cd ~/Desktop/projects/hauz-frontend-take-home && cat > src/shared/theme.ts <<'EOF'
/**
 * Three states, not two, which is what makes this worth storing at all.
 *
 * `system` is a real answer: it means "follow the device", and it is the
 * default. Only an explicit choice is written down, and only an explicit choice
 * overrides prefers-color-scheme. Collapsing this to a boolean would force
 * everyone into a decision they never made.
 */
export type Theme = 'system' | 'light' | 'dark'

export const THEME_LABELS: Record<Theme, string> = {
  system: 'Auto',
  light: 'Light',
  dark: 'Dark',
}

export function parseTheme(raw: unknown): Theme {
  return raw === 'light' || raw === 'dark' || raw === 'system' ? raw : 'system'
}

/** Auto, then the two explicit choices, then back to letting the device decide. */
export function nextTheme(current: Theme): Theme {
  if (current === 'system') return 'light'
  if (current === 'light') return 'dark'
  return 'system'
}
EOF
cat >> src/server/cookies.ts <<'EOF'

/**
 * Not a secret, but stored the same way as everything else so there is one
 * place cookies are written. Kept server-side for a reason: read during SSR it
 * settles the theme before the first byte of HTML, which is the same trick the
 * header uses and rules out the flash of the wrong palette on a hard refresh.
 */
const THEME = 'hauz_theme'
const THEME_MAX_AGE = 365 * 24 * 60 * 60

export function writeThemeCookie(theme: string) {
  setCookie(named(THEME), theme, options(THEME_MAX_AGE))
}

export function readThemeCookie() {
  return getCookie(named(THEME))
}
EOF
```

```
import type { QueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import {
  HeadContent,
  Outlet,
  Scripts,
  createRootRouteWithContext,
  useRouteContext,
} from '@tanstack/react-router'

import { SiteHeader } from '#/components/site-header'
import { loadShell } from '#/server/session'
import appCss from '../styles.css?url'

export interface RouterContext {
  queryClient: QueryClient
}

export const Route = createRootRouteWithContext<RouterContext>()({
  head: () => ({
    meta: [
      { charSet: 'utf-8' },
      { name: 'viewport', content: 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1' },
      { title: 'HAUZ' },
    ],
    links: [
      // Loaded at runtime, not at build time, so a slow or blocked font host
      // delays glyphs and nothing else. Both families have a real fallback
      // stack in the stylesheet.
      { rel: 'preconnect', href: 'https://fonts.googleapis.com' },
      {
        rel: 'preconnect',
        href: 'https://fonts.gstatic.com',
        crossOrigin: 'anonymous',
      },
      {
        rel: 'stylesheet',
        href: 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Fraunces:opsz,wght@9..144,400;9..144,500;9..144,600&family=Schibsted+Grotesk:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap',
      },
      { rel: 'stylesheet', href: appCss },
    ],
  }),

  // This HTML names the person looking at it, so it is not something a CDN or
  // proxy may keep and hand to whoever asks next.
  headers: () => ({ 'Cache-Control': 'private, no-store' }),

  // Runs on the server while the page is being rendered, before any HTML
  // exists. That is what makes both the header and the palette right on the
  // first paint rather than corrected after hydration. Every child route reads
  // this same value, so no two parts of the page can disagree.
  beforeLoad: async () => await loadShell(),

  component: RootLayout,
  shellComponent: RootDocument,
})

/**
 * Anything that depends on route context belongs here rather than in the shell
 * below: the shell also wraps the error and not-found components, which render
 * in situations where the context this needs may never have been produced.
 */
function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <>
      <SiteHeader />
      <Outlet />
    </>
  )
}

function RootDocument({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const { theme } = useRouteContext({ from: '__root__' })

  return (
    // Only an explicit choice is stamped. Leaving the attribute off for
    // `system` is what lets prefers-color-scheme decide, which is the whole
    // point of having three states rather than a boolean.
    <html lang="en" data-theme={theme === 'system' ? undefined : theme}>
      <head>
        <HeadContent />
      </head>
      <body>
        {children}
        <Scripts />
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

```bash
 * The six icons this app actually uses, drawn here rather than pulled from a
 * package. An icon library would add a dependency and a few hundred kilobytes
 * of shapes nobody renders, to save writing these lines once.
 *
 * All of them share one grid and one stroke weight so they sit together, and
 * all take their colour from `currentColor` so they work in both themes without
 * being told which one they are in. They are decorative: every control that

 * assistive technology.

type IconProps = {
```

```bash
import { createServerFn } from '@tanstack/react-start'
import { z } from 'zod'

import { writeLocaleCookie, writeThemeCookie } from '#/server/cookies'

/**
 * Appearance and language, both stored server-side for the same reason: they
 * have to be known before the first byte of HTML. Kept in the browser and
 * applied after hydration, each would flash its old value on every hard
 * refresh, and the language would arrive too late for `<html lang>`.
 */

export const setTheme = createServerFn({ method: 'POST' })
  .validator((data: unknown) =>
    z.object({ theme: z.enum(['system', 'light', 'dark']) }).parse(data),
  )
  .handler(async ({ data }) => {
    writeThemeCookie(data.theme)
    return { ok: true } as const
  })

export const setLocale = createServerFn({ method: 'POST' })
  .validator((data: unknown) =>
    z.object({ locale: z.enum(['uz', 'ru', 'en']) }).parse(data),
  )
  .handler(async ({ data }) => {
    writeLocaleCookie(data.locale)
    return { ok: true } as const
  })
```

Now the header — a segmented theme switcher plus a language picker, with icons:

```
import { Link, useRouteContext, useRouter } from '@tanstack/react-router'
import { useState } from 'react'

import {
  ChevronDownIcon,
  GlobeIcon,
  LogOutIcon,
  MonitorIcon,
  MoonIcon,
  SunIcon,
} from '#/components/icons'
import { setLocale, setTheme } from '#/server/preferences'
import { signOut } from '#/server/session'
import {
  LOCALES,
  LOCALE_LABELS,
  LOCALE_SHORT,
  translator,
  type Locale,
} from '#/shared/i18n'
import { THEMES, type Theme } from '#/shared/theme'

const THEME_ICONS: Record<Theme, typeof SunIcon> = {
  system: MonitorIcon,
  light: SunIcon,
  dark: MoonIcon,
}

/**
 * Reads what the root route resolved during SSR, so all of this renders
 * correctly in the very first HTML rather than after hydration. Fetching the
 * person in an effect would paint "Sign in" and correct it a moment later,
 * which is the flash the brief rules out.
 */
export function SiteHeader() {
  const { viewer, theme, locale } = useRouteContext({ from: '__root__' })
  const router = useRouter()
  const [leaving, setLeaving] = useState(false)
  const t = translator(locale)

  // Both preferences live in cookies the server reads, so the page is
  // re-resolved rather than patched in the browser. That is also what stops a
  // later hard refresh from flashing the setting they just left.
  async function chooseTheme(next: Theme) {
    if (next === theme) return
    await setTheme({ data: { theme: next } })
    await router.invalidate()
  }

  async function chooseLocale(next: Locale) {
    if (next === locale) return
    await setLocale({ data: { locale: next } })
    await router.invalidate()
  }

  async function handleSignOut() {
    if (leaving) return
    setLeaving(true)

    try {
      await signOut()
      // Re-runs the root beforeLoad. Without it the header keeps rendering the
      // person who just left.
      await router.invalidate()
      await router.navigate({ to: '/' })
    } finally {
      setLeaving(false)
    }
  }

  return (
    <header>
      <Link to="/" className="brand">
        HAUZ
      </Link>

      <div className="tools">
        {/* Three states shown as three targets. A cycling button hides two of
            them behind guesswork about what comes next. */}
        <div className="segmented" role="group" aria-label={t('nav.appearance')}>
          {THEMES.map((option) => {
            const Icon = THEME_ICONS[option]
            return (
              <button
                key={option}
                type="button"
                aria-pressed={option === theme}
                aria-label={t(`theme.${option}`)}
                title={t(`theme.${option}`)}
                onClick={() => chooseTheme(option)}
              >
                <Icon />
              </button>
            )
          })}
        </div>

        <div className="select">
          <GlobeIcon />
          <select
            aria-label={t('nav.language')}
            value={locale}
            onChange={(event) => chooseLocale(event.target.value as Locale)}
          >
            {LOCALES.map((option) => (
              <option key={option} value={option}>
                {LOCALE_SHORT[option]} · {LOCALE_LABELS[option]}
              </option>
            ))}
          </select>
          <ChevronDownIcon size={14} />
        </div>
      </div>

      {viewer.state === 'ready' && (
        <>
          <span className="who">{viewer.account.firstName}</span>
          <button type="button" onClick={handleSignOut} disabled={leaving}>
            <LogOutIcon />
            {leaving ? t('nav.loggingOut') : t('nav.logOut')}
```

```
/*
 * One stylesheet, no framework, no utility classes. Mostly written against
 * semantic elements, with a handful of class names where the markup genuinely
 * has two kinds of the same element.
 *
 * The direction is the one property marketplaces have actually settled on:
 * cool neutral ground, white cards, a near-black primary action, and a single
 * blue reserved for links, focus and selection. One sans family, no display
 * serif. The restraint is the design; anything that draws attention here is
 * taking it from the listing.
 *
 * Themes come in three states, not two. An explicit choice puts `data-theme` on
 * the root element and wins over the system. Choosing nothing leaves no
 * attribute at all, and prefers-color-scheme decides. Every colour is a token
 * defined on bare :root and redefined per theme, so nothing is ever left with
 * one theme's text on the other theme's ground.
 */

:root {
  --bg: #fafafa;
  --surface: #ffffff;
  --surface-2: #f4f4f5;
  --ink: #09090b;
  --ink-2: #3f3f46;
  --muted: #6b6b74;
  --border: #e4e4e7;
  --border-strong: #d4d4d8;

  --accent: #2563eb;
  --accent-hover: #1d4ed8;
  --accent-weak: #eff4ff;

  --primary: #18181b;
  --primary-hover: #2f2f35;
  --primary-ink: #fafafa;

  --danger: #b42318;
  --danger-weak: #fef3f2;

  --radius: 10px;
  --radius-sm: 8px;
  --radius-pill: 999px;

  --font: 'Geist', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;

  color-scheme: light dark;
  font-family: var(--font);
  font-size: 15px;
  line-height: 1.55;
  -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
}

@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root:not([data-theme='light']) {
    --bg: #09090b;
    --surface: #131316;
    --surface-2: #1b1b1f;
    --ink: #fafafa;
    --ink-2: #d4d4d8;

    --danger-weak: #2a1512;

}
```

```bash
feat: Uzbek, Russian and English, and a redesign that looks like a product

Two things, and they turn out to be the same thing: both the language and the
palette have to be settled on the server, before any HTML exists.

The language lives in a cookie and is resolved in the same round trip as the
signed-in person. Picked in the browser and applied after hydration it would
flash the wrong language on every hard refresh, and it would arrive too late
for `<html lang>`, which screen readers and translation tools read before any

lang="ru" in the first response, with no JavaScript involved.

server does not own the reader's language, so it says what went wrong and the
browser says it in the language they chose. Field-level issues still arrive
from the Function in English; translating those would mean the Function
knowing the locale, which is a larger change than this task wants.

tool reaches for, not the one property marketplaces use. This is the one they
actually use: cool neutral ground, white cards, a near-black primary action,
and a single blue held back for links, focus and selection. One sans family and
no display face. Colour is for what can be followed, not for decoration.

Appearance is three targets rather than a cycling button, which hid two states
behind a guess about what came next. The chosen one is painted from its own
token so it reads as raised in both themes rather than pressed in under dark.
```

## Claude

Your criticism was justified and I will say it plainly: I had fallen into **warm cream + display serif + one decorative accent** — which is exactly the look a generative tool picks, not the one real proptech companies use. I have redone it.

\## The new direction — how real products do it

| Before (the AI look) | Now |
|---|---|
| Warm cream `#FBF8F2` | **A cool neutral** `#FAFAFA` + white cards |
| A display serif (Fraunces) | **Geist** — one sans family, no serif |
| A coloured primary button | A **near-black** button — the current standard pattern |
| The accent as decoration | Blue **only** for links, focus and selection |
| Cream hairlines | Clean `#E4E4E7` borders, almost no shadow |

The rule is simple: **colour is for things you can click**, not for decoration.

\## Language — UZ / RU / EN

This is not just a select. The language is **resolved in a cookie, under SSR**, exactly like the header:

```
hauz_locale=ru → <html lang="ru"> + the Russian text in the FIRST HTML
```

Two reasons: picked in the browser, the wrong language flashes for an instant on every hard refresh; and for `<html lang>` it is **far too late** — screen readers and translation tools read it **before** our code runs.

Along with that, **the server no longer returns an English sentence — it returns a code**. The server does not know the reader's language: it says *what happened*, and the browser *says it* in the chosen language. That is an architectural decision and it is worth stating in the interview.

*(An honest limitation: field errors coming from the Function stay in English — translating them would require the Function to know the language, which is outside the scope of the task. I will write it into NOTES.md.)*

\## Theme — 3 targets, not a cycling button

The previous button required you to guess the next state. Now it is a **segmented control**: monitor / sun / moon. The selected one is painted from **its own token** — so it reads as brighter in the dark theme, not pressed in. I found and fixed that from a screenshot.

\## Icons — drawn, not installed

7 inline SVGs. Adding a library would have meant one dependency and hundreds of shapes nobody renders. All on one grid, one stroke weight, `currentColor` — so none of them needs to know which theme it is in.

\## Verified

Both themes seen in the browser ✓ · the RU translation under SSR ✓ · the `lang` attribute correct ✓ · `npm run verify` passes ✓ · the email hides on a narrow screen ✓

What is left is **`NOTES.md` and `README.md`** — items 3 and 2 of the brief and the part that earns the most marks. Shall I write them?

```bash
/**

 *     back, Tab closes rather than walking into a floating list
 *   - closed means `visibility: hidden`, which takes the rows out of the tab
 *     order for real instead of merely hiding them, while still allowing the
 *     open and close to animate

 *
 * It renders closed on the server and stays closed through hydration, so there
```

## Claude

Both controls are now identical — **our own dropdown, with animation**.

\## The look

The trigger: the current selection plus its own icon (monitor/sun/moon, globe). A pill shape, a soft background on hover, and when open the border changes to the accent and the **chevron rotates 180°**.

The menu: it opens from `translateY(-6px) scale(.97)` with `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`, a soft shadow, a blue ✓ on the selected row.

\## But let me state the cost

The native `<select>` was **free and correct** — I replaced it because you asked. The moment you start drawing the menu yourself, the platform door closes and you have to **rebuild by hand everything it was doing quietly**. That is exactly where custom dropdowns break. I did build it:

| What | State |
|---|---|
| `aria-haspopup` / `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` | ✓ announced as a collapsed listbox |
| `role="listbox"` + `aria-selected` | ✓ reads "2 of 3, selected" |
| Enter / Space / ↓ → opens on the current selection | ✓ |
| ↑↓ wrap, Home/End jump | ✓ **tested in the browser** |
| Escape closes **and returns focus** | ✓ **tested in the browser** |
| Tab closes it (you cannot tab into a floating list) | ✓ |
| `visibility: hidden` when closed | ✓ the rows **really** leave the tab order, and the animation survives |
| Clicking outside closes it | ✓ |

An important detail: the **active** (arrow-key) and **selected** (✓) states are distinguished. Walking down the list must not look like it is changing the setting.

You saw it in the screenshot: after Escape the blue focus ring appeared on the trigger — focus was not lost.

You have filled in onboarding — the header now shows a **name**, the home page says "View your profile", and opening `/onboarding` sends you to `/`. So requirement 2 and its gate work fully.

```bash
 * So it goes through the query cache, which is already in the router's context
 * for exactly this. Fresh for half a minute, which is long enough to cover
 * moving around the app and short enough that a session revoked elsewhere is
 * noticed soon.
 *
 * Anything that changes who is signed in has to clear it, which is what
 * `refreshShell` is for. Calling `router.invalidate()` alone would re-run the
 * loader against a cache that still holds the person who just signed out.
 */
export const SHELL_QUERY_KEY = ['shell'] as const

export function shellQueryOptions() {
  return {
    queryKey: SHELL_QUERY_KEY,
    queryFn: () => loadShell(),
    staleTime: 30_000,
  }
}

export async function refreshShell(router: AnyRouter, queryClient: QueryClient) {
  await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: SHELL_QUERY_KEY })
  await router.invalidate()
}
```

## Claude

The cause of the freeze was found and measured.

\## The problem

Changing the theme **went to Appwrite twice**:

```
account.get            324 ms
function execution     490 ms
──────────────────────────────
viewer total           814 ms
cookie read            0.0 ms   ← the only thing actually needed
```

The cookie was written → then the whole root loader was re-run → and it asked "who is signed in?". But **picking a colour does not change who you are**.

\## The fix

Preferences now live in context, seeded from the server. On selection:
1. state updates **immediately**
2. the attribute on `<html>` is set by hand (after hydration it is not React's)
3. the cookie is written **in the background** — nobody waits

SSR still emits `data-theme` and `lang` in the first render, so there is no flash on a hard refresh. Confirmed in the browser: **no pause**, and it survived a full reload.

Along the way: **the shell now goes through the query cache**. 814 ms is worth paying to know who is signed in, but paying it **every time** while moving between four screens is too much. When the session changes the cache is cleared through one helper (`router.invalidate()` on its own would have left the just-signed-out person in the cache).

\## The page design

You were right — `/signin` read as a skeleton. Fixed:

- **Centred** — a single-purpose screen should not be stuck under the header
- **The house mark** + a heading + an explanation
- **"Step 1 / 2"** — a form that grows into a second screen reads as an error if it does not say so
- The "Different email" button is **quieter** than the primary next to it — it is a way back, not a second action
- The note about spam only appears while a code is expected
- **A real CTA button** on the home page, not a link inside a sentence

Onboarding is centred too. All the text is in all three languages.

---

The code side is fully done. **What is left is two files:** `NOTES.md` and `README.md` — items 2 and 3 of the brief, and NOTES.md is the file that earns the most marks. It will carry your decisions on the 6 traps, the `QueryClient` bug in the starter, the `validateSearch` finding and the measured perf numbers.

Shall I write it?

```bash
# One scope: sessions.write
#
# The starter README asks for four. Measured against this project, three of
# them are not reachable from this app:
#   users.read       the Users service is never called; the signed-in person is

#   execution.write  the Function is invoked with the caller's session, never
#                    with this key, because its execute access is `users`
#
# The key is used in exactly one place: account.createSession, in
# src/server/auth.ts. A wider key is a wider blast radius for no gain.
APPWRITE_API_KEY=""")
```

```bash
The only change to the Function.

Its update schema told anyone who emptied a first name to "send null to clear
this field, not an empty string". First and last name are not nullable, so null
would have been rejected too. The advice was sound for contact email and bio,
```

```
# Notes

## How it is put together

Every Appwrite call happens on the server. The browser holds an `HttpOnly`
cookie carrying the session secret and nothing else; there is no Appwrite SDK,
no key and no secret in the client bundle, and `npm run verify` greps the built
output to keep it that way.

The root route resolves the signed-in person, their Personal Account, the theme
and the language in one round trip before any HTML exists. That is what makes
the header correct on the first paint instead of corrected after hydration, and
it is why `<html lang>` and `data-theme` are already right on a hard refresh.

Profile data only moves through the Function. That is not just discipline: the
table is pushed with no permissions, and the API key carries no row scopes, so
the app could not reach it directly if it tried.

## Where I did not follow the brief

**The `redirect` parameter.** Sending people wherever it points is an open
redirect. `?redirect=https://hauz-uz.com/login` lets someone sign in on the real
domain and land on a copy asking them to sign in again. Only internal paths are
honoured; everything else goes home. (`e821737`)

**Sending the user id with the profile form.** That makes identity something the
client asserts, and anything asserted can be edited. On a marketplace that is a
realtor's contact address and every enquiry meant for them. The form sends no
id; the Function already takes the caller from `x-appwrite-user-id`, which
Appwrite injects and will not accept from a caller. (`2b4a4f4`)

**"If loading the current user fails for any reason, treat them as signed
out."** A timeout, a 502 mid-deploy and a 429 are not an invalid session.
Following this would turn a few seconds of Appwrite being unwell into a forced
sign-out for everyone holding a good session. Only 401 and 403 clear the cookie;
anything else reports `unknown`, which keeps the session and lets the UI say it
does not know rather than say something false. (`2a6e9d3`)

## What I found in the starter

`src/router.tsx` built the `QueryClient` at module scope. Start creates a router
per SSR request, so one process-wide cache could serve one visitor's rows in
another visitor's HTML. Moved inside `getRouter`. (`7de55a0`)

The README asks for four API key scopes. Measured, one is enough:
`createEmailToken` created a fresh account with `sessions.write` alone, the
`Users` service is never called, and the Function runs on the caller's session
rather than the key. Reasons are in `.env.example`.

**The only change to the Function** (`3eafd38`): its update schema told anyone
who emptied a first name to send `null` instead. First and last name are not
nullable, so `null` fails too. That advice is right for contact email and bio
and a dead end for the other two, which now say they are required.

## What I measured instead of assuming

- `createEmailToken` returns the six digit code in the response body when called
  with an API key. Step one of sign-in therefore runs unauthenticated, so the
  code exists only in the inbox. Step two must use the key, because the session
  secret is only returned to a key request — which is the single reason the key
  needs `sessions.write` at all.
- `validateSearch` runs and returns the cleaned value, while `Route.useSearch()`
  still hands the component the raw one. The redirect guard was in the wrong
  place and looked right. Sanitising now happens at every point of use.
- Two rows with the same owner: `409 row_unique_constraint_violation`. The
  "double-click cannot make two accounts" rule holds in the index, not in the
  disabled button.
- Changing the theme cost 814ms, because it re-resolved the viewer
  (`account.get` 324ms, Function 490ms) to read back a cookie. Preferences now
  apply locally and the cookie is written in the background. (`0fbc36a`)
- Empty string against `null` against absent: eight cases through the patch
  builder, including an emptied required field and a whitespace-only edit.

## Past the brief

Styling, three languages and the appearance setting are more than was asked
for — the brief says unstyled is fine. None of it touched the Function or the
rules above, and the language work paid for itself: server functions now return
error codes rather than English sentences, because the server does not own the
reader's language.

## Next, for production

- Replace the redirect shape check with an allowlist of returnable routes.
- Add a test runner. `buildPatch`, `safeRedirect` and the Function response
  mapping were checked with throwaway scripts; they should be committed tests.
- Pass the locale to the Function so field-level `issues` arrive translated.
  They are English today, which is the one place the language stops.
- Back off on 429 and give "resend code" a cooldown; Appwrite rate limits and
  the UI currently just reports it.
- Narrow the deployed key to `sessions.write`, and rotate it on a schedule.
```

```
# HAUZ frontend take-home

Sign-in, onboarding and profile for a property marketplace, built on the
starter in `TASK.md`. This file is about getting it running. The decisions, and
the places I did not follow the brief, are in `NOTES.md`.

## What you need

- Node 22 or newer
- A free Appwrite Cloud account at https://cloud.appwrite.io

## Setup

Roughly 15 minutes, most of it waiting for the Function to build.

### 1. Install dependencies

`‌``bash
npm install
`‌``

### 2. Create an Appwrite project

In the Appwrite Console, create a new project. From **Overview**, copy the
**Project ID** and the **API Endpoint**. The endpoint is region specific, for
example `https://fra.cloud.appwrite.io/v1`.

Put both into `appwrite.config.json`, replacing the `projectId` and the
`endpoint` if your region differs.

### 3. Push the database, table and Function

`‌``bash
npx appwrite login
npm run appwrite:push
`‌``

That creates the `main` database, the `personal_accounts` table with its unique
index, and deploys the `personal-account` Function. The first deployment takes a
minute or two.

Confirm it worked: the Function should appear under **Functions** with a ready
deployment, and its **Execute access** should be `users`.

> `appwrite push table` treats `appwrite.config.json` as the whole schema and
> deletes tables that are not in it. Safe on the fresh project you just made.
> Never run it against a project that has anything else in it. To redeploy only
> the Function later, use `npx appwrite push function --all --force`.

### 4. Create an API key

Console, **Overview**, **Integrations**, **API keys**, **Create API key**.

One scope: **`sessions.write`**.

The starter asked for four. Measured against this project the other three are
never reached, and the reasoning is written out in `.env.example`. The key is
used in exactly one call, `account.createSession`.

Copy the secret once. You cannot read it again.

### 5. Fill in your environment

`‌``bash
cp .env.example .env
`‌``

Fill in `APPWRITE_ENDPOINT`, `APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID` and `APPWRITE_API_KEY`.
`.env` is git-ignored. Do not commit it.

### 6. Run it

`‌``bash
npm run dev
`‌``

http://localhost:3000

## Trying it out

Sign in with any email you can read. Appwrite Cloud sends the code from its own
mail server on the free plan, so check your spam folder; if nothing arrives
after a few minutes it may be rate limiting you, so wait rather than clicking
send repeatedly.

Worth a look while you are in there:

- Hard refresh while signed in. The header is right in the first paint, not
  corrected afterwards.
- Open `/profile` signed out. It signs you in and comes back to `/profile`.
- Try `/signin?redirect=https://example.com`. It goes to the home page.
- Put something in the bio, save, clear it, save, then reload. It stays gone.
- Appearance and language are in the header. Both are resolved on the server,
  so a hard refresh does not flash the previous one.

## Scripts

`‌``bash
npm run dev            development server on :3000
npm run build          production build
npm run typecheck      tsc --noEmit
npm run verify         typecheck, build, then check the client bundle
npm run check:client   fail if anything server-only reached the browser
npm run generate-routes
npm run appwrite       the Appwrite CLI, scoped to this project's config
`‌``

`check:client` is the first rule of the task turned into a check rather than a
habit: it scans the built client output for the server SDK, for Appwrite
credential headers, and for the literal value of `APPWRITE_API_KEY`. It is worth
running before pushing, because the safe import and the unsafe one look
identical at the import site.

## What is in here

`‌``
src/
  routes/                 the four screens, plus the root shell
  components/             header, menu, icons, preferences
  server/                 everything that talks to Appwrite; never imported by a component
… (32 more lines)
```

The log revealed the problem: **`notFoundError` on route `__root__`**. The cause — I had used `redirect({ href })`; it worked server-side (with curl), but on a client navigation the router could not resolve the path and produced a notFound.

The sequence was: the code **was accepted correctly** → the session was created → the move to `/onboarding` produced notFound → you saw "it did not go anywhere". On the second press the pending cookie had already been cleared → "expired".

The fix — an **allowlist** instead of a shape check, which at the same time makes `to` type-safe:

**Ran** — Replace shape-only check with a typed allowlist

```bash
cd ~/Desktop/projects/hauz-frontend-take-home && python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('src/shared/redirect.ts'); s = p.read_text()

s = s.replace(""" * In production this would be better still as a list of the routes that are
 * worth returning to. There are four of them; the shape check is what stays
 * correct as that grows.
 */
export function safeRedirect(raw: unknown): string {""",
""" * The shape check alone is not the whole answer, and a bug made that concrete:
 * a checked path is still only a string, and handing a string to the router as
 * `href` produced a not-found instead of a navigation. So the check ends in a
 * list of the routes worth returning to. The result is one of two literals,
 * which means the router can be given `to` and TypeScript verifies the
 * destination exists.
 *
 * `/signin` and `/onboarding` are deliberately not returnable; sending someone
 * back to where they just came from is a loop, not a courtesy.
 */
const RETURNABLE = ['/', '/profile'] as const

export type ReturnTo = (typeof RETURNABLE)[number]

export function safeRedirect(raw: unknown): ReturnTo {""")

s = s.replace("""  if (!path.startsWith('/')) return '/' // absolute URL, or a scheme
  if (path.startsWith('//')) return '/' // protocol relative: resolves off-site
  if (path.includes('\\\\')) return '/' // some parsers read this as a slash
  if (path.includes('://')) return '/' // a scheme smuggled past the first check
  if (/[\\u0000-\\u001f\\u007f]/.test(path)) return '/' // control chars, CRLF

  return path
}""",
"""  if (!path.startsWith('/')) return '/' // absolute URL, or a scheme
  if (path.startsWith('//')) return '/' // protocol relative: resolves off-site
  if (path.includes('\\\\')) return '/' // some parsers read this as a slash
  if (path.includes('://')) return '/' // a scheme smuggled past the first check
  if (/[\\u0000-\\u001f\\u007f]/.test(path)) return '/' // control chars, CRLF

  // The shape is fine. Now: is it somewhere we actually return people to?
  const route = path.split(/[?#]/)[0]

  return RETURNABLE.includes(route as ReturnTo) ? (route as ReturnTo) : '/'
}""")

s = s.replace("""export function redirectParam(raw: unknown): string | undefined {""",
"""export function redirectParam(raw: unknown): ReturnTo | undefined {""")
p.write_text(s)

# onboarding: href -> to
p = pathlib.Path('src/routes/onboarding.tsx'); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace("""      // `href`, not `to`: the destination is data, not one of the literal
      // route paths the router knows at compile time.
      throw redirect({ href: next })""",
"""      // `to`, because safeRedirect narrows to a route the router knows. This
      // was `href` and a bare string, which the router answered with a
      // not-found rather than a navigation.
      throw redirect({ to: next })""")
s = s.replace("await router.navigate({ href: next })", "await router.navigate({ to: next })")
p.write_text(s)
… (3 more lines; the file is in the repo)
```

## Claude

Fixed and pushed.

\## What had happened

Your code **was accepted correctly** — the session was created and the one-time code spent. Then the move to `/onboarding` produced a `notFound` and you saw "it did not go anywhere". On the second press the pending cookie had already been cleared → from the outside that looks **exactly like "expired"**.

The cause: I had written `redirect({ href: next })`. `href` is a string the router resolves **at runtime**, and it resolved to nothing. `to` is a path the router knows **at compile time**.

\## The most important lesson — my test had passed

When I requested `/profile` while signed out I got `307 → /signin?redirect=%2Fprofile` and counted it as "works". But that was a redirect **on the server** — it goes through a **different path** than the router. The client navigation was never tested. **A green test over a broken flow.**

You found it by using the app, I did not. It is written into `agent-log/mistakes.md` as entry 6, framed that way — the most valuable kind for the brief.

\## The fix — it strengthened the defence at the same time

`safeRedirect` no longer returns "a string that looked safe". After the shape check the result is matched against **a list of two routes worth returning to**, and its type is the union of those two literals — so the router is given `to` and TypeScript checks the destination exists.

`/signin` and `/onboarding` are **not** in the list — sending someone back to the place they just came from is a loop. 15 cases tested, those two included.

Along the way a **404 page** was added (in three languages) — the router had been warning about it, and without this specific bug it would have shown a bare "Not Found".

---

Confirm — then I will run the bio-clearing loop end to end.

## Claude

\# Audit — as a testing engineer

**The short answer: do not submit yet.** The code is ready, but there are **two blockers** and both are yours.

---

\## 🔴 Blocker 1 — we are not meeting a brief requirement

`agent-log/sessions/` is **empty**. Item 4 of the brief asks for *"your agent prompts or exported agent sessions"*. The mistakes list (6 entries, with commit links) is ready; **the sessions are not**. That is an unmet requirement, not a quality question.

\## 🔴 Blocker 2 — two flows have never been tested end to end

- **Sign-in** — there was a bug yesterday, I fixed it, but **you have not tested it yet**
- **Clearing the bio** — the logic passes 8/8 unit tests, but the full loop against the real Function has not been run. I wrote in the README that it "works" — that is still **an unverified claim**

A green test has already hidden a broken flow once. It must not be allowed to happen a second time.

---

\## Audit results — what was tested

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `typecheck` + `build` + bundle | ✓ passed |
| Secrets in the SSR HTML (`secret`, the key, the endpoint) | ✓ 0 occurrences |
| `node-appwrite` / the key in the client bundle | ✓ absent (9 files, 420 KB) |
| Open redirect — 9 attack variants | ✓ all to `/` |
| `/signin`, `/onboarding` not return targets | ✓ no loop |
| The route gates (while signed out) | ✓ 307 + `redirect` preserved |
| The 404 page | ✓ in three languages |
| i18n coverage | ✓ 60/60 keys, in all three languages, no dead keys |
| A11y: label↔input, listbox ARIA, `aria-hidden` SVG, `lang` | ✓ complete |
| Unused exports | ✓ none |
| The Function deployment | ✓ live |

\## What the audit found — fixed

**There was no `errorComponent`.** This mattered because it **contradicted our own philosophy**: we built the `unknown` state precisely so we could say "we do not know, but your session is fine" — yet if the RPC itself failed the user saw TanStack's raw error screen, which reads like a catastrophe and pushes them to sign in again for nothing. Now it says, in three languages, that you have not been signed out, and offers a retry button.

---

\## The UI/UX verdict

**The brief says "unstyled is fine".** You went beyond that — which is **the right call**, but only on one condition: that the things being graded did not suffer. They did not — and I said so openly in `NOTES.md`, because a reviewer might otherwise wonder "did they misjudge the priorities?".

**Strengths:** cool neutral + a near-black primary button — the language of real proptech, not an AI cliché. The menus **work fully** with a keyboard (Escape returns focus — I tested it). The icons are drawn, no library added. Both themes from one token set.

**Weaknesses in the UI — honestly:**

1. **The home page looks empty.** That is deliberate: I did not fabricate listings. But it may read as sparse to a reviewer.
2. **The mouse moves focus in the menu** (`onMouseEnter` → `focus`). Many menus do this, but it can cause a jump when keyboard and mouse are mixed.
3. **The `preferences` context is seeded from the server once.** Change the language in another tab and this tab does not know. Not noticeable in practice.
4. **No loading states.** A navigation can take 814 ms (the first time) — there is no skeleton or progress.

None of these is a blocker.

---

\## Final state against the requirements

```
✓ 2 Onboarding                       ✓ 5 Log out (both ways)
✓ 3 Profile + returning to /profile
✓ Rule 1 no secret in the browser (with an automatic check)
✓ Rule 2 only through the Function (the key has no row scopes)

✓ 30 commits, not squashed
✓ NOTES.md (1 page) · README.md updated
✓ agent-log/mistakes.md — 6 entries, with commit links
⬜ agent-log/sessions/ — EMPTY
⬜ end-to-end confirmation of sign-in and the bio
⬜ repo private + HAUZ's access
```

---

\## The order before submitting

1. **Sign in** → the name appears in the header → **hard refresh** → no flash
2. Tell me — I run **the bio loop** in the browser
3. Export the conversation into `agent-log/sessions/`
4. Confirm the repo is **private**

After that it can be submitted. Submit now and item 4 is unmet — and that is exactly the discipline item the brief deliberately checks.

## Claude

Fixed and pushed — **31 commits**.

\## The home page

It now shows the **real data** that exists: the full name, the role (as a pill), the contact email and the bio, plus an "Edit profile" link.

An important detail: **an optional field that was not filled in looks different** — grey and italic. Writing "not provided" with the same weight as a real answer makes the record **harder** to read, not easier.

I did not add fabricated listings — they would have said less than what is genuinely stored.

\## The three weaknesses the audit found — fixed

**1 · There was no loading indicator.** Resolving a route means an Appwrite call plus a Function execution (we measured it — 814 ms). Clicking during that time looked like "nothing happened". Now there is a thin accent line at the top — quiet to the point of being unnoticeable, but a click no longer looks swallowed.

**2 · The mouse stole focus in the menu.** Hover moved the highlight **and the focus** together — so someone typing who brushed the list had the caret pulled away. Now the highlight follows the mouse and **focus follows the keyboard only**.

**3 · A dead translation key** (`onboarding.intro`) removed. Now **all 60 keys are used and present in all three languages** — verified with a script.

\## What I deliberately did not fix — and why

The `preferences` context is seeded from the server **once**, so changing the language in another tab leaves this tab unaware. The fix looks easy (sync when the props change), but it is **dangerous**: if something calls `refreshShell` after a theme selection while the cookie write has not landed yet, the context returns the old value and your choice **reverts**. An invisible regression — more expensive than the real benefit. It is left in `NOTES.md`.

```
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react'

/**
 * Six digits, six boxes.
 *
 * One field would have been less code. It would also have been worse at the one
 * job it has: a code copied out of an email arrives with spaces, a non-breaking
 * space or a stray newline, phones offer the wrong keyboard for a text input,
 * and a wrong digit in the middle of a six character string is hard to find.
 *
 * So the value stays a single string and the boxes are a view onto it. That
 * keeps the form simple — one piece of state, the same string the server
 * validates — while the boxes handle what people actually do:
 *
 *   - typing fills forward, one box at a time
 *   - backspace on an empty box steps back and clears the one before
 *   - arrow keys move without editing
 *   - pasting anywhere fills everything, and survives spaces, dashes and the
 *     non-breaking space that mail clients like to insert
 *   - autocomplete="one-time-code" lets iOS and Android offer the code from the
 *     SMS or mail app, which only works if the first box carries it
 *   - a complete code submits, because asking someone to reach for a button
 *     after the last digit is asking for nothing
 */

const LENGTH = 6

/** Anything that is not a digit is noise, wherever it came from. */
function digitsOnly(text: string) {
  return text.replace(/\D/g, '').slice(0, LENGTH)
}

export function CodeInput({
  id,
  value,
  onChange,
  onComplete,
  disabled,
  describedBy,
}: {
  id: string
  value: string
  onChange: (next: string) => void
  onComplete?: (code: string) => void
  disabled?: boolean
  describedBy?: string
}) {
  const boxes = useRef<Array<HTMLInputElement | null>>([])
  const digits = value.padEnd(LENGTH, ' ').slice(0, LENGTH).split('')

  // The caret belongs on the first box that is still empty, so typing always
  // continues where it left off rather than wherever the pointer last landed.
  const cursor = Math.min(value.length, LENGTH - 1)

  useEffect(() => {
    if (value.length === LENGTH) onComplete?.(value)
    // onComplete is called for a finished code, not on every keystroke.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [value])

  function focusBox(index: number) {
    boxes.current[Math.max(0, Math.min(index, LENGTH - 1))]?.focus()
  }

  function setDigit(index: number, digit: string) {
    const next = value.padEnd(LENGTH, ' ').split('')
    next[index] = digit
    onChange(next.join('').replace(/\s+$/, '').trimEnd())
  }

  return (
    <div className="code" role="group" aria-describedby={describedBy}>
      {Array.from({ length: LENGTH }, (_, index) => (
        <input
          key={index}
          id={index === 0 ? id : `${id}-${index}`}
          ref={(node) => {
            boxes.current[index] = node
          }}
          type="text"
          inputMode="numeric"
          // Only the first box advertises it, or the browser offers to fill
          // each box with the whole code.
          autoComplete={index === 0 ? 'one-time-code' : 'off'}
          aria-label={`${index + 1} / ${LENGTH}`}
          maxLength={1}
          disabled={disabled}
          value={digits[index]?.trim() ?? ''}
          onFocus={(event) => {
            event.target.select()
            if (index > cursor) focusBox(cursor)
          }}
          onChange={(event) => {
            const typed = digitsOnly(event.target.value)
            if (!typed) return
            // A paste can land in onChange rather than onPaste on some
            // browsers; treat more than one digit as a fill.
            if (typed.length > 1) {
              onChange(typed)
              focusBox(typed.length)
              return
            }
            setDigit(index, typed)
            focusBox(index + 1)
          }}
          onKeyDown={(event) => {
            if (event.key === 'Backspace') {
              event.preventDefault()
              if (digits[index]?.trim()) {
                setDigit(index, ' ')
                onChange(value.slice(0, index))
              } else if (index > 0) {
                onChange(value.slice(0, index - 1))
                focusBox(index - 1)
              }
            } else if (event.key === 'ArrowLeft') {
              event.preventDefault()
              focusBox(index - 1)
            } else if (event.key === 'ArrowRight') {
              event.preventDefault()
```

```
import { useMutation } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { createFileRoute, useRouter } from '@tanstack/react-router'
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { useState } from 'react'

import { CodeInput } from '#/components/code-input'
import { HomeIcon } from '#/components/icons'
import { usePreferences } from '#/components/preferences'
import { refreshShell } from '#/lib/shell'
import { requestSignInCode, verifySignInCode } from '#/server/auth'
import { redirectParam, safeRedirect } from '#/shared/redirect'

export const Route = createFileRoute('/signin')({
  // Declares the shape, and nothing more. It is tempting to sanitise here and
  // be done, but measured against this version of the router that does not
  // hold: validateSearch runs and returns the cleaned value, while
  // Route.useSearch() still hands the component the raw one. Every read below
  // goes through safeRedirect for that reason.
  validateSearch: (search: Record<string, unknown>): { redirect?: string } =>
    typeof search.redirect === 'string' ? { redirect: search.redirect } : {},
  component: SignIn,
})

/**
 * One screen, two steps. New and returning people see the same thing, because
 * Appwrite creates the account the first time it sees an address, so there is
 * nothing for the UI to branch on.
 *
 * Only the step lives in component state. The user id that ties the two
 * requests together stays in an HttpOnly cookie, so there is nothing on this
 * page for the browser to tamper with and a refresh mid-flow strands nobody.
 */
function SignIn() {
  const router = useRouter()
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  const { t } = usePreferences()
  // Cleaned on the way out of the URL, never trusted as read.
  const next = safeRedirect(Route.useSearch().redirect)

  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [code, setCode] = useState('')
  const [sentTo, setSentTo] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)

  /**
   * A rejected mutation means the call never completed: the network dropped, or
   * the server function could not be reached. Without this the promise is
   * rejected into nothing and the form simply sits there, which is worse than
   * an error, because the person cannot tell whether it worked.
   */
  function reportFailure(cause: unknown) {
    console.error('[signin]', cause)
    setError(t('error.unreachable'))
  }

  const request = useMutation({
    mutationFn: (address: string) =>
      requestSignInCode({ data: { email: address } }),
    onError: reportFailure,
    onSuccess: (result, address) => {
      if (!result.ok) {
        setError(t(`error.${result.code}`))
        return
      }
      setError(null)
      setCode('')
      setSentTo(address)
    },
  })

  const verify = useMutation({
    mutationFn: (entered: string) =>
      verifySignInCode({ data: { code: entered } }),
    onError: reportFailure,
    onSuccess: async (result) => {
      if (!result.ok) {
        setError(t(`error.${result.code}`))
        // The parked user id is gone, so there is nothing left to redeem. Send
        // them back to the start rather than leaving them typing into a step
        // that can no longer succeed.
        if (result.code === 'expired') {
          setSentTo(null)
          setCode('')
        }
```

## Claude

**Bug found — in the component I wrote myself.** I typed `866095` and the boxes showed `6 0 5`. The cause: when typed fast, each keystroke relies on React's **stale** value (a stale closure) — digits are lost. It only shows up with fast typing or automation. I am rewriting it:

**Created** `~/Desktop/projects/hauz-frontend-take-home/src/components/code-input.tsx`

```
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react'

/**
 * Six digits, six boxes.
 *
 * One field would have been less code. It would also have been worse at the one
 * job it has: a code copied out of an email arrives with spaces or a
 * non-breaking space, phones offer the wrong keyboard for a text input, and a
 * wrong digit in the middle of a six character string is hard to spot.
 *
 * The value stays one string and the boxes are a view onto it, so the form
 * holds a single piece of state and the server validates the same thing the
 * person sees. Index `i` shows `value[i]`; there are never gaps, because typing
 * only ever fills left to right.
 *
 * Every handler reads and writes `latest` rather than the `value` prop. React
 * batches state updates, so during fast typing — or a paste that arrives as
 * six separate key events — each handler would otherwise see the value from
 * before the previous keystroke and overwrite it. That is not theoretical:
 * typing "866095" quickly produced "605".
 */

const LENGTH = 6

/** Anything that is not a digit is noise, wherever it came from. */
function digitsOnly(text: string) {
  return text.replace(/\D/g, '').slice(0, LENGTH)
}

export function CodeInput({
  id,
  value,
  onChange,
  onComplete,
  disabled,
}: {
  id: string
  value: string
  onChange: (next: string) => void
  onComplete?: (code: string) => void
  disabled?: boolean
}) {
  const boxes = useRef<Array<HTMLInputElement | null>>([])
  const latest = useRef(value)

  // Keeps the ref honest when the value changes from outside, such as the form
  // clearing it after a wrong code.
  useEffect(() => {
    latest.current = value
  }, [value])

  useEffect(() => {
    if (value.length === LENGTH) onComplete?.(value)
    // Fires for a finished code, not for every keystroke.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [value])

  function commit(next: string) {
    latest.current = next
    onChange(next)
  }

  function focusBox(index: number) {
    boxes.current[Math.max(0, Math.min(index, LENGTH - 1))]?.focus()
  }

  function handleDigit(index: number, digit: string) {
    const current = latest.current

    // Replace in place, or append if they are at the end of what is typed.
    const next =
      index < current.length
        ? current.slice(0, index) + digit + current.slice(index + 1)
        : (current + digit).slice(0, LENGTH)

    commit(next)
    focusBox(index + 1)
  }

  function handleBackspace(index: number) {
    const current = latest.current

    if (current[index]) {
      commit(current.slice(0, index) + current.slice(index + 1))
      return
    }

    if (index > 0) {
      commit(current.slice(0, index - 1) + current.slice(index))
      focusBox(index - 1)
    }
  }

  function handleFill(text: string, from: number) {
    const digits = digitsOnly(text)
    if (!digits) return

    const current = latest.current
    const next = (current.slice(0, from) + digits).slice(0, LENGTH)

    commit(next)
    focusBox(next.length)
  }

  return (
    <div className="code" role="group">
      {Array.from({ length: LENGTH }, (_, index) => (
        <input
          key={index}
          id={index === 0 ? id : `${id}-${index}`}
          ref={(node) => {
            boxes.current[index] = node
          }}
          type="text"
          inputMode="numeric"
          // Only the first box advertises it, or the browser offers to put the
          // whole code into every box.
          autoComplete={index === 0 ? 'one-time-code' : 'off'}
          aria-label={`${index + 1} / ${LENGTH}`}
          maxLength={1}
… (41 more lines)
```

```bash
import pathlib
```

```bash
cd ~/Desktop/projects/hauz-frontend-take-home && python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('agent-log/mistakes.md'); s = p.read_text()
entry = """## 7. Wrote every mutation without a failure path

**What it wrote.** Three screens, seven `useMutation` calls, and not one
`onError` between them. Every one handled the case where the server answered
with a refusal, and none handled the case where the call never completed.

**How I caught it.** I did not. Signing in froze: the code was accepted,
nothing moved, and a second attempt said the code had expired. The server log
showed no error for that attempt at all, because the failure was on the client
and it had nowhere to go. An earlier entry in the same log named the likely
cause — `Invalid server action param for serverFnId`, a page left open across
enough hot reloads that its server function ids had gone stale.

**Why it matters.** A rejected promise with no handler is a dead form. The
person cannot tell whether it worked, so they try again, and the second attempt
reports an expired code because the first one really did spend it. The bug is
invisible in development, where you reload without thinking, and it is the
first thing a reviewer would hit on a page left open.

**Fix.** Every mutation now has `onError`. It logs the cause and says the
server could not be reached, which is both true and actionable. The navigation
after a successful sign-in is wrapped too, so "you are signed in but we could
not open the page" is a thing the app can say rather than a thing it does.
Commit `<errors>`.

---

## 8. A six box code input that dropped digits

**What it wrote.** Each box wrote the whole code back through `onChange` on
every keystroke, computing the next value from the `value` prop.

**How I caught it.** Typing `866095` into it. The boxes showed `605`.

**Why it matters.** React batches state updates, so each keystroke in a fast
burst read the value from before the previous one and overwrote it. Typing at a
normal speed by hand mostly hides it; a paste delivered as key events, an
autofill, or anyone typing quickly does not. I would not have found this by
reading the code, and neither would a reviewer.

**Fix.** Handlers read and write a ref that is updated synchronously, so each
keystroke sees what the one before it did. Retested with the same six digits,
end to end, through a real sign-in. Commit `<errors>`.

---

"""
s = s.replace("<!--\nStill to record", entry + "<!--\nStill to record")
p.write_text(s)
print("7 va 8 qo'shildi")
```

## Claude

The bug is found and fixed. **I ran the whole flow end to end myself** — it works.

\## It was actually three separate defects

**1 · The root cause: no `onError` on the mutations.** **Seven** `useMutation`s across three screens, and not one of them handled the case where the call **never arrived at all**. A rejected promise with no handler is **a dead form**: nothing appears, the person cannot tell whether it worked, they press again — and the second attempt says "expired", because **the first one really did spend the code**.

There was no error on the server because the failure was on the client and **had nowhere to go**. The log hints at the cause: `Invalid server action param for serverFnId` — the page had been left open through too many HMR reloads and the server function ids had gone stale.

**2 · My new code input lost digits.** I typed `866095` — the boxes showed `605`. React batches state updates, so when typing fast each keystroke read the value from **before the previous one** and wrote over it. Typing slowly by hand hides it; paste, autofill or fast typing do not. **This could not have been found by reading the code.**

**3 · There was no gate on `/signin`.** A signed-in person could sit in the sign-in form while seeing their own name in the header — which reads as a broken session.

\## The copy was wrong too

You were right: saying "valid for 15 minutes" and then "expired" is misleading. The code had actually been **spent**; no time had passed. Now: *"This code no longer works — it has been used or has expired. Request a new one."*

\## The OTP input — done properly

Six boxes, **digits only**, `inputMode="numeric"` (the numeric keypad on a phone), `autocomplete="one-time-code"` on the first box only (otherwise the browser would try to put the whole code into every box).

**Paste works** — paste into any box and it fills from the start, stripping spaces, dashes and the **non-breaking spaces** mail clients insert. Backspace steps back from an empty box, the arrows move without editing, and the code **submits itself** once complete.

\## Confirmed

I entered the code `[REDACTED: one-time code]` in the browser → all six digits landed correctly → it submitted automatically → **it went to `/onboarding`** ✓ · the `/signin` gate works ✓ · `npm run verify` passes ✓

`agent-log/mistakes.md` now has **8 entries**. Number 7 is the one you found — "the silent freeze". 33 commits.

> **A note:** a page left open a long time goes stale after HMR. It will no longer "freeze" — it now says *"We could not reach the server"*. Refreshing the page is enough.

## Claude

**Bug found, and the cause is clear too.** Onboarding saved and went to `/` — but the home page still says "Finish setting up your account" and the header shows the email rather than the name.

The cause: `ensureQueryData` returns data from the cache even when it is **marked stale** — it only issues a request when the data is **absent entirely**. And `invalidateQueries` only marks it "stale".

**Ran** — Remove the cached shell instead of marking it stale

```bash
cd ~/Desktop/projects/hauz-frontend-take-home && python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('src/lib/shell.ts'); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace(""" * Anything that changes who is signed in has to clear it, which is what
 * `refreshShell` is for. Calling `router.invalidate()` alone would re-run the
 * loader against a cache that still holds the person who just signed out.
 */""",
""" * Anything that changes who is signed in has to clear it, which is what
 * `refreshShell` is for. Calling `router.invalidate()` alone would re-run the
 * loader against a cache that still holds the person who just signed out.
 *
 * It removes the entry rather than invalidating it, and the difference is the
 * whole point. `invalidateQueries` marks data stale; `ensureQueryData` hands
 * back whatever is cached and only fetches when there is nothing there. So an
 * invalidate followed by a route resolution returned the same answer as before:
 * finishing onboarding landed on a home page still asking you to onboard, with
 * your email in the header instead of your name. Removing it leaves nothing to
 * hand back, so the next resolution has to ask.
 */""")
s = s.replace("""export async function refreshShell(router: AnyRouter, queryClient: QueryClient) {
  await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: SHELL_QUERY_KEY })
  await router.invalidate()
}""",
"""export async function refreshShell(router: AnyRouter, queryClient: QueryClient) {
  queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: SHELL_QUERY_KEY })
  await router.invalidate()
}""")
p.write_text(s)
print("ok")
PY
```

This is **your window**, frozen in the "Saving…" state — the request never finished.

Part of the cause is mine: while I am editing files the dev server reloads and **cuts off in-flight requests** (the `ECONNRESET` in the log). But underneath there is a real defect: **a request that never finishes freezes the UI forever** — there is no timeout at all.

**Ran** — Give every server call a deadline

```bash
cd ~/Desktop/projects/hauz-frontend-take-home && cat > src/lib/timeout.ts <<'EOF'
/**
 * A server call that never answers.
 *
 * Every mutation here handles a refusal and a rejection, but a request that
 * simply hangs is neither: the promise stays pending, the button stays on
 * "Saving…", and there is no way out but a reload. It happens for ordinary
 * reasons — a connection dropped mid-flight, a dev server restarting under an
 * in-flight request — and from the other side it looks like the app died.
 *
 * So calls are given a deadline. Passing it is reported the same way a network
 * failure is, because to the person waiting they are the same thing.
 */
const DEFAULT_MS = 20_000

export class TimeoutError extends Error {
  constructor(ms: number) {
    super(`No answer within ${ms}ms`)
    this.name = 'TimeoutError'
  }
}

export function withTimeout<T>(work: Promise<T>, ms = DEFAULT_MS): Promise<T> {
  return new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new TimeoutError(ms)), ms)

    work.then(
      (value) => {
        clearTimeout(timer)
        resolve(value)
      },
      (cause) => {
        clearTimeout(timer)
        reject(cause)
      },
    )
  })
}
```
